result.title: Fractional physics-informed neural networks to model social media virality
result.summary: Existing models of social media virality either prescribe the functional form of engagement growth or assume a fixed mechanism by which past activity influences future engagement. We present a fractional physics-informed neural network that learns both the temporal memory and nonlinear growth dynamics of social media engagement, using symbolic regression to translate the learned dynamics into interpretable equations. Synthetic experiments at the deployment resolution of 24 hourly observations demonstrate that the fractional order and reaction law can be jointly recovered from clean data. Under observation noise, however, the standard pointwise physics residual drives the fractional order toward its lower bound through a scale artifact. We address this failure using a fully whitened residual that propagates observation noise through the fractional operator. Applying the framework to 348 posts from X (formerly Twitter), we find that a single-window model estimates strongly memory-dependent dynamics but fails to accurately reconstruct held-out trajectories. Partitioning the 24-hour window into four teacher-forced segments substantially improves performance, yielding segment-specific fractional orders that increase from 0.23 to 0.99 and interpretable growth laws for each phase. The segmented model reconstructs 64% of held-out trajectories within a mean squared error of 0.01, compared with 44% for the strongest of nine classical baselines. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of fractional physics-informed equation discovery to uncover interpretable engagement dynamics while highlighting the importance of noise-aware estimation and temporal segmentation.

AI.brief_summary: 用分数阶物理信息神经网络联合学习社媒参与度的时间记忆与非线性增长律，以符号回归导出可解释方程；针对观测噪声下点式物理残差导致的分数阶下界伪影提出白化残差，并对 348 条推文做 24 小时窗口的分段建模。
AI.relevance_reason: 分数阶记忆算子与噪声白化残差可能为 latent 状态更新中的长程记忆先验和含噪监督提供线索，分段 teacher-forcing 也可供核查多阶段推理状态的分段训练，但原文不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
